# 4 Maccabees Chapter 9 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The First Brothers Tortured and Killed

---

**1** When Antiochus was convinced that he had been outwitted by their refusal, he commanded the instruments of torture to be brought in.

**2** When the rack and the rest of the torture equipment had been set up, the tyrant commanded that the tongue of the spokesman be cut out, that he be scalped, and that his hands and feet be cut off, while the other brothers and their mother looked on.

**3** After he had been thus mutilated in all his limbs, Antiochus commanded that he be brought still breathing to the fire and roasted.

**4** As the vapor of the burning spread all around, the brothers together with the mother urged one another on to die nobly, saying:

**5** The Lord God sees all things, and in truth he is compassionate toward us, as Moses declared in his song of testimony: And he will have compassion on his servants.

**6** When the first had died in this manner, they brought the second brother for mockery; and after they had torn the skin from his head with its hair, they asked him: Will you eat before your entire body is punished limb by limb?

**7** He answered in the language of his fathers: No!

**8** And so he also underwent the successive torments.

**9** When the second too had died worthily, the third was brought forward and questioned in the same manner.

**10** He answered: I will not deny the blessed law of God nor will I betray the nobility of my brothers. I will endure everything.

**11** After he had been put on the rack and his arms had been torn away, he was brought to the wheel while they continued to call to him: Renounce your impiety and we will have mercy on you!

**12** But he answered: Your wheel is not powerful enough to take from me the eternal life. Cut my body, for you cannot touch my soul with all your instruments of torture.

**13** When Antiochus and his attendants saw that this young man could not be persuaded either, they had him brought to the fire alive, commanding his brothers and the mother to watch.

**14** But the mother and the brothers encouraged one another to die for the law, saying to one another in the ancestral tongue:

**15** The Lord God looks upon us, and truly he has compassion on us, as Moses declared in the song of testimony: And he will have compassion on his servants.

**16** And when the first had died, the others each in turn declared the same courage.

**17** The first, having persevered in his suffering unto death, said: I will endure every kind of pain for the sake of the soul that has hope in God.

**18** The second said: Do you not realize, murderer, that in proportion as you torment us, you yourself are being tormented more?

**19** The third, when commanded to put out his tongue, immediately stretched it out and fearlessly extended his hands, saying:

**20** From heaven I received these; for the sake of God's laws I disdain them; and from him I hope to receive them back again.

**21** So that even the king and those with him were amazed at the young man's spirit, that he regarded his sufferings as though they were nothing.

**22** When he too had died, the fourth was tortured in the same manner.

**23** When he was near death, he said: It is better for those who die at God's hand to cherish hope of a divine resurrection. For you, however, there will be no resurrection to life.

**24** After this they brought forward the fifth and maltreated him.

**25** He looked at the king and said: Since you have authority among people, you do as you please, though you yourself are mortal. But do not suppose that God has forsaken our people.

**26** Just continue on your present course, and see how his great power will torture you and your descendants.
